subject: ss-gastroenterology
title: Diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy: an exam-focused overview

steps.tx: Endoscopic resection is used for early neoplasia. **Endoscopic mucosal resection** (EMR) removes lesions confined to the mucosa, often after lifting with submucosal injection and snaring. **Endoscopic submucosal dissection** (ESD) uses a knife to dissect the submucosa, allowing en bloc removal of larger or fibrotic lesions. ESD has higher perforation risk and longer procedure time than EMR.

steps.tx: **ERCP** (endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography) treats stones, strictures and leaks in the biliary and pancreatic ducts. Its most feared complication is **post-ERCP pancreatitis**, which is lessened by rectal non-steroidal anti-inflammatory suppositories and by placing a **pancreatic duct stent** in high-risk patients. Other key complications include **bleeding**, **perforation** and **cholangitis**. Ascending cholangitis with shock needs urgent biliary drainage.
steps.say: ERCP treats stones, strictures and leaks within the bile and pancreatic ducts. The complication you must not miss is pancreatitis after the procedure. Rectal anti-inflammatory suppositories and a pancreatic duct stent in higher-risk patients reduce that risk. Bleeding, perforation and infection in the bile ducts are the other main concerns. A patient with cholangitis and shock needs the bile duct drained urgently.

rows: Most common and most feared; reduced by rectal anti-inflammatory suppositories and pancreatic stenting in high-risk patients
Often follows sphincterotomy; usually controlled with endoscopic haemostasis
Can be duodenal or biliary; needs prompt recognition and treatment
Ascending infection; with shock, urgent biliary drainage is required

steps.tx: **Endoscopic ultrasound** (EUS) gives the most accurate local staging for oesophageal, pancreatic and rectal cancers. **EUS-guided fine needle aspiration or biopsy** samples lesions adjacent to the gut wall, such as pancreatic masses and lymph nodes. Enteral stents and **PEG tubes** provide palliation for obstruction and feeding access respectively. PEG is placed by a pull or push technique through the anterior abdominal wall.

steps.tx: Capsule endoscopy is the main test for **obscure GI bleeding** after negative upper and lower endoscopy. It is purely diagnostic, with no biopsy or haemostasis. In suspected strictures, as in Crohn's disease, a **patency capsule** should be given first to exclude **capsule retention**, which occurs in about 2.6 percent of Crohn's patients. Symptomatic retention needs endoscopic or surgical removal.
